mainTopic: Megillah 31b: special readings for אב and fast days, the merit of the מעמדות and קרבנות, reading the קללות, and where the weekly Torah readings resume
overview: This amud first covers the special readings of the month of אב. When ראש חודש אב falls on שבת, the הפטרה is 'חדשיכם ומועדיכם'. On תשעה באב itself, several opinions are given, and אביי reports the custom: 'כי תוליד בנים' with the הפטרה 'אסוף אסיפם'. The גמרא then explains why the מעמדות read מעשה בראשית: the world stands because of the קרבנות. A dialogue between אברהם and הקדוש ברוך הוא teaches that when there is no בית המקדש, reading the סדר קרבנות counts like bringing them. Next, the גמרא explains why the קללות are not split on a תענית, and אביי limits that rule to the curses in ויקרא. A story about רב הונא shows this rule in practice. A ברייתא then teaches that עזרא set the curses before עצרת and ראש השנה so that the year ends with its curses. After a teaching about following elders, with רחבעם as the example, the amud ends with a מחלוקת between רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה about where the weekday Torah readings resume. It closes with רבי זירא's ruling and a question about his wording, which is answered on the next amud.

steps.title: The הפטרה when ראש חודש אב falls on שבת
steps.stepSummary: When ראש חודש אב falls on שבת, the הפטרה is the section from ישעיה that includes 'חדשיכם ומועדיכם'.
steps.simpleTranslation: When ראש חודש אב falls on שבת, the הפטרה is the passage containing 'Your New Moons and your Festivals My soul hated; they were a burden to Me.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא states a rule about the הפטרה for a שבת that is also ראש חודש אב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally ראש חודש on שבת has its own special הפטרה. In the month of mourning, a rebuke passage is chosen instead. The verse fits because it mentions ראש חודש ('חדשיכם') in a negative tone.

keyTerms.meaning: The first day of the month of Av
They read as the הפטרה (reading from the Prophets)

phrases.english: The New Moon of Av
that falls on Shabbat,
they read as the haftara
"Your New Moons and your Festivals My soul hated;
they were a burden to Me."

steps.triggerLanguage: רֹאשׁ חֹדֶשׁ אָב שֶׁחָל לִהְיוֹת בְּשַׁבָּת, מַפְטִירִין
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When ראש חודש אב falls on שבת, the הפטרה is 'חדשיכם ומועדיכם' (ישעיה א).
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens this passage with a new הפטרה rule.

steps.title: What does 'a burden to Me' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the words 'היו עלי לטורח' mean.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'they were a burden to Me' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pauses to ask what the verse means. This sets up the explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Calling something a 'burden' to the הקדוש ברוך הוא is hard to understand, since He is never tired. The גמרא wants to know what kind of burden is meant.

phrases.english: What is meant by "they were a burden to Me"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about a phrase in the verse quoted in step 1.

steps.title: Israel sins and then makes God reconsider the punishment
steps.stepSummary: The הקדוש ברוך הוא says: not only do they sin, they also 'trouble' Me to figure out which harsh decree to bring on them.
steps.simpleTranslation: הקדוש ברוך הוא said: It is not enough for ישראל that they sin before Me. They also burden Me to work out which harsh decree I should bring upon them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the 'burden': Israel sins, which calls for punishment, and then prays, which pushes God to reconsider.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The burden is not physical effort. It is the back-and-forth of having to judge a people that sins and also begs for mercy. This explains why the passage suits the mourning period of אב.

keyTerms.meaning: The Holy One, Blessed be He
It is not enough for them

phrases.english: The Holy One, Blessed be He, said:
It is not enough for Israel
that they sin before Me,
but they also burden Me
to work out which harsh decree
I shall bring upon them.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא: לֹא דַּיָּין לָהֶם לְיִשְׂרָאֵל
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The 'burden' is that Israel sins and then makes God reconsider which decree to bring.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 2.

steps.title: Which הפטרה is read on תשעה באב itself?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which הפטרה is read on the day of תשעה באב.
steps.simpleTranslation: On תשעה באב itself, what do we read as the הפטרה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves from ראש חודש אב to the fast day itself. It sets up a question that רב will answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'גופיה' ('itself') signals a contrast with the earlier case. Before, the topic was ראש חודש in the month of mourning. Now it is the actual day of mourning.

keyTerms.meaning: The fast of the Ninth of Av

phrases.english: On the Ninth of Av itself,
what do we read as the haftara?

steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which הפטרה is read on תשעה באב.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the ראש חודש אב case to the fast day itself.

steps.title: רב: 'How did she become a harlot'
steps.stepSummary: רב says the הפטרה on תשעה באב is 'איכה היתה לזונה' (ישעיה א:כא).
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: The הפטרה is the passage 'How has [the faithful city] become a harlot.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב answers that the הפטרה is the passage from ישעיה beginning 'איכה היתה לזונה'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This passage continues the same chapter of ישעיה used in step 1. Its opening word 'איכה' also matches the mournful mood of the day, the same word that opens מגילת איכה.

keyTerms.meaning: A harlot (here a metaphor for an unfaithful city)

phrases.english: Rav said:
"How has she become a harlot."

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The הפטרה on תשעה באב is 'איכה היתה לזונה'.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 4.

steps.title: Which Torah reading is used on תשעה באב?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which Torah portion is read on תשעה באב.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the Torah reading?
steps.whatsHappening: Having settled the הפטרה, the גמרא now asks about the Torah reading. This sets up a ברייתא with several opinions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here 'מקרא' means the reading from the Torah itself, as opposed to the הפטרה from the Prophets.

phrases.english: What is the Torah reading?

steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which Torah portion is read on תשעה באב.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the הפטרה to the Torah reading.

steps.title: A ברייתא with three opinions on the Torah reading
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא records three views: אחרים say 'ואם לא תשמעו לי' (the curses in ויקרא). רבי נתן בר יוסף says 'עד אנה ינאצוני' (the spies). יש אומרים say 'עד מתי לעדה הרעה' (also the spies).
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: Others say the reading is 'But if you will not listen to Me.' רבי נתן בר יוסף says it is 'How long will this people provoke Me.' And some say it is 'How long shall I bear with this evil congregation.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a ברייתא that lists three different opinions about the Torah reading.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion picks the תוכחה, the warning of punishments. The other two pick verses from the sin of the spies (מרגלים), which happened on תשעה באב. Those two differ only on which verse in במדבר יד the reading should start from.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in a ברייתא

phrases.english: It was taught: Others say:
"But if you will not listen to Me",
Rabbi Natan bar Yosef says:
"How long will this people provoke Me",
And some say:
"How long [shall I bear] with this evil congregation."

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Three opinions: the תוכחה in ויקרא, or one of two verses from the episode of the spies.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 6 with a ברייתא.

steps.title: אביי: the custom nowadays
steps.stepSummary: אביי reports that the accepted practice is to read 'כי תוליד בנים' (דברים ד) and to use 'אסוף אסיפם' (ירמיה ח) as the הפטרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: Nowadays everyone is accustomed to read 'When you shall have children,' and the הפטרה is 'I will utterly consume them.'
steps.whatsHappening: אביי closes the discussion by reporting the custom that people actually follow, for both the Torah reading and the הפטרה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Despite the earlier opinions, the common custom became a different set of readings. 'כי תוליד בנים' warns of exile, and 'אסוף אסיפם' describes destruction. This is the custom still followed today on the morning of תשעה באב.
steps.whatToRemember: On תשעה באב, the halacha follows אביי's custom: the Torah reading is 'כי תוליד בנים' and the הפטרה is 'אסוף אסיפם'.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the practice still followed today on the morning of תשעה באב.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix this up with רב's 'איכה היתה לזונה' (step 5). In practice, many communities read that passage as part of the הפטרה for שבת חזון, not on תשעה באב itself.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
Nowadays everyone is accustomed
to read "When you shall have children",
and they read as the haftara "I will utterly consume them."

steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The practice is to read 'כי תוליד בנים' with the הפטרה 'אסוף אסיפם'.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the actual custom after the opinions in steps 5 and 7.

steps.title: Back to the משנה: the מעמדות read מעשה בראשית
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה: the מעמדות read מעשה בראשית.
steps.simpleTranslation: [The משנה says:] In the מעמדות they read מעשה בראשית, etc.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to quote a new line of the משנה. This sets up the question that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The מעמדות were groups of ordinary Jews who stood by while the קרבנות were offered on behalf of their region. Back in their home towns, they read the account of Creation.

keyTerms.meaning: The non-priestly 'watches' tied to the Temple offerings

phrases.english: [In the watches they read] the account of Creation, etc.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic by quoting the משנה.

steps.title: Why do the מעמדות read מעשה בראשית?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where this practice comes from.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where are these matters derived?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the reason or source behind the משנה's rule. This sets up רבי אמי's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The connection between the מעמדות and the creation of the world is not obvious. The גמרא wants that link explained.

phrases.english: From where are these matters derived?

steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason the מעמדות read מעשה בראשית.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the משנה line quoted in step 9.

steps.title: רבי אמי: the world exists because of the מעמדות
steps.stepSummary: רבי אמי says that without the מעמדות, heaven and earth would not endure. He proves it from 'אם לא בריתי יומם ולילה'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אמי said: Were it not for the מעמדות, heaven and earth would not endure, as it says: 'If not for My covenant day and night, I would not have set the laws of heaven and earth.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אמי explains that the world's existence depends on the Temple service. That is why the מעמדות read about Creation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'covenant day and night' is read as the daily קרבנות, offered morning and evening. Since Creation is kept going through the עבודה, the people tied to that עבודה read the account of Creation.

keyTerms.meaning: רבי אמי, an אמורא from ארץ ישראל
Would endure or continue to exist

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the עבודה, and the people standing with it, are seen as holding up the whole world, not only as a local ritual.

phrases.english: Rabbi Ami said:
Were it not for the watches,
heaven and earth would not endure,
as it is stated:
"If not for My covenant day and night,
I would not have set the laws of heaven and earth."

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The world exists in the merit of the מעמדות and the daily offerings, so they read about Creation.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 10.

steps.title: אברהם asks: במה אדע?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings the verse 'במה אדע כי אירשנה'. It explains that אברהם was asking whether Israel might be wiped out like דור המבול and דור הפלגה if they sinned.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it is written: 'And he said, Lord God, by what shall I know that I shall inherit it?' אברהם said before הקדוש ברוך הוא: רבונו של עולם, perhaps, Heaven forbid, ישראל will sin before You, and You will do to them as to דור המבול and דור הפלגה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a second verse and a story about אברהם that supports רבי אמי's idea that the קרבנות protect the world. This step only sets up the question; the full answer comes in the next lines.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אברהם is not doubting God's promise. He is worried that sin could cause Israel to be destroyed completely. The answer, given in steps 13–17, will point to the קרבנות (and later the reading of the סדר קרבנות) as what protects Israel.

keyTerms.meaning: The generation of the Dispersion (Tower of Bavel)

phrases.english: And it is written:
"And he said, Lord God,
by what shall I know that I shall inherit it?"

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר אַבְרָהָם לִפְנֵי הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא:
phrases.english: Abraham said before the Holy One, Blessed be He:
Master of the Universe,
perhaps, Heaven forbid,
Israel will sin before You
and You will do to them
as to the generation of the Flood and the generation of the Dispersion?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּכְתִיב: ״וַיֹּאמַר ה׳ אֱלֹהִים בַּמָּה אֵדַע כִּי אִירָשֶׁנָּה״
steps.raayaObject: רבי אמי's idea that the offerings sustain the world and protect Israel.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The verse 'במה אדע כי אירשנה' (בראשית טו:ח) and the related דרשה.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second verse to strengthen the theme of step 11.

steps.title: God answers: No
steps.stepSummary: The הקדוש ברוך הוא tells אברהם that He will not destroy Israel the way He destroyed those generations.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: No.
steps.whatsHappening: God gives אברהם a first answer: no, Israel will not be wiped out. The conversation continues next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This short 'no' establishes that Israel will not be totally destroyed. אברהם will next ask how he can be sure, and the answer will lead to the קרבנות.

phrases.english: He said to him: No.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: God will not destroy Israel as He did דור המבול and דור הפלגה.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אברהם's question in step 12.

steps.title: אברהם asks how he can be sure
steps.stepSummary: אברהם asks the הקדוש ברוך הוא: by what will I know that my children will not be wiped out?
steps.simpleTranslation: אברהם said before Him: רבונו של עולם, 'By what shall I know?'
steps.whatsHappening: The story from the last step continues. אברהם asks a follow-up question: what will protect his children?
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 13 the הקדוש ברוך הוא promised not to destroy Israel the way He destroyed דור המבול and דור הפלגה. Now אברהם wants to know how that will work. If Israel sins, what will save them?

keyTerms.meaning: Master of the World, a way of speaking to ה׳
By what shall I know? (בראשית ט״ו:ח)
He said before Him, a respectful way of saying he spoke to ה׳

phrases.english: He (Abraham) said before Him:
Master of the World, 'By what shall I know?'
phrases.notes: Here the verse is read as: by what merit will my children survive?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לְפָנָיו: רִבּוֹנוֹ שֶׁל עוֹלָם, בַּמֶּה אֵדַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows the promise in step 13 by asking how the protection will work.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What will protect Israel from destruction if they sin?

steps.title: The answer is קרבנות
steps.stepSummary: The הקדוש ברוך הוא answers with the verse about bringing animals. This hints that קרבנות will bring כפרה for Israel.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: 'Take Me a three-year-old calf, etc.'
steps.whatsHappening: ה׳ answers אברהם with the next verse, which tells him to take animals for an offering. The message is that קרבנות will atone for Israel.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא reads the verse 'קחה לי עגלה משולשת' as the answer to 'במה אדע'. The animals stand for the קרבנות that Israel will bring in the future. Those קרבנות will bring כפרה, so Israel will not be destroyed.

keyTerms.meaning: etc., the rest of the verse

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לוֹ: ״קְחָה לִי עֶגְלָה מְשׁוּלֶּשֶׁת וְגוֹ׳״.
phrases.english: He said to him: 'Take Me a three-year-old calf, etc.'
phrases.notes: Meaning: through קרבנות they will gain atonement.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ: קְחָה לִי עֶגְלָה מְשׁוּלֶּשֶׁת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אברהם's question from step 14.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: קרבנות will bring כפרה and protect Israel.

steps.title: What about when there is no Temple?
steps.stepSummary: אברהם pushes back: קרבנות only work while the בית המקדש stands. What will happen when it is gone?
steps.simpleTranslation: He said before Him: רבונו של עולם, that works when the בית המקדש stands. When the בית המקדש does not stand, what will become of them?
steps.whatsHappening: אברהם points out a problem with the answer. Without a בית המקדש, there are no קרבנות, so how will Israel get כפרה?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer in step 15 depended on קרבנות being brought. אברהם challenges how far that answer reaches: it covers only the time of the בית המקדש. Something else is needed for the long years of גלות.

keyTerms.meaning: that works out well, that is fine

phrases.english: He said before Him: Master of the World,
this works out well at a time when the Temple stands.
At a time when the Temple does not stand,
what will become of them?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges how far the answer in step 15 reaches.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that קרבנות will protect Israel
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: קרבנות need a בית המקדש, so the answer does not cover the time after the Temple is destroyed.

steps.title: Reading about קרבנות counts like bringing them
steps.stepSummary: The הקדוש ברוך הוא says He has already set up the סדר קרבנות. When Israel reads it, He counts it as if they brought a קרבן, and He forgives them.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: I already set up for them the order of offerings. Whenever they read them, I count it as if they brought an offering before Me, and I forgive all their sins.
steps.whatsHappening: ה׳ gives the final answer. Even without a בית המקדש, learning the parts of the Torah about קרבנות brings כפרה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This closes the gap from step 16. Reading the פרשיות of קרבנות takes the place of actually bringing them. This also ties back to the משנה: reading Torah, like the מעמדות reading מעשה בראשית, holds up the world.

keyTerms.meaning: the order of offerings, the Torah passages about קרבנות
I have set up, I have established

steps.whatToRemember: The whole aggadah: the world stands because of the מעמדות and קרבנות. When there is no בית המקדש, reading the סדר קרבנות counts as bringing them and brings כפרה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This גמרא is a well-known source for saying the פרשיות of קרבנות in davening every day.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לוֹ: כְּבָר תִּקַּנְתִּי לָהֶם סֵדֶר קׇרְבָּנוֹת,
phrases.english: He said to him: I have already set up for them the order of offerings.
Whenever they read them,
I count it for them
as if they brought an offering before Me,
and I forgive all their sins.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves אברהם's challenge from step 16.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Reading the סדר קרבנות counts like bringing קרבנות and brings forgiveness.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Learning about קרבנות protects Israel even in גלות.

steps.title: The משנה: blessings and curses on fast days
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה. On fast days we read the ברכות וקללות, and we do not split up the קללות.
steps.simpleTranslation: On fast days, the blessings and curses are read, and we do not interrupt in the curses.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic by quoting the next line of the משנה. It is setting up a question about where this rule comes from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On a תענית we read the ברכות וקללות of פרשת בחוקותי (ויקרא כ״ו). 'אין מפסיקין' means we do not stop in the middle of the קללות to switch to a new עולה. One person reads all of them.

keyTerms.meaning: the blessings and curses in the Torah
we do not interrupt (do not split between two readers)

steps.confusionAlert: 'אין מפסיקין' does NOT mean we skip the קללות. They are read, but one person reads them all in a single aliyah.

phrases.english: On fast days, the blessings and curses are read,
and we do not interrupt in the curses.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the aggadah to the next line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On fast days the ברכות וקללות are read, and the קללות are not split between readers.

steps.title: Where does this rule come from?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source of the rule not to interrupt the קללות.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where are these words derived?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the source of the rule just quoted. This sets up the answers that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is about the second half of the משנה: why may the קללות not be split up? The גמרא wants a reason or a verse.

keyTerms.meaning: From where are these words? (asking for a source)

phrases.english: From where are these words derived?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the rule in step 18.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source for not interrupting the קללות.

steps.title: Do not despise ה׳'s rebuke
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא בר גמדא in the name of רבי אסי brings the verse 'מוסר ה׳ בני אל תמאס'. Stopping in the middle of the קללות looks like disgust with ה׳'s rebuke.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא בר גמדא said in the name of רבי אסי: Because the verse says, 'The rebuke of ה׳, my son, do not despise.'
steps.whatsHappening: The first answer brings a verse from משלי. We must not look like we are running away from ה׳'s rebuke.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Stopping in the middle of the קללות makes it look like we cannot stand to hear them. That shows disrespect for ה׳'s מוסר, so we read them all at once.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר גַּמָּדָא אָמַר רַבִּי אַסִּי:
phrases.english: Rabbi Chiya bar Gamda said in the name of Rabbi Asi:

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר קְרָא ״מוּסַר ה׳ בְּנִי אַל תִּמְאָס״.
phrases.english: For the verse says: 'The rebuke of ה׳, my son, do not despise.'

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר קְרָא מוּסַר ה׳ בְּנִי אַל תִּמְאָס
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 19 with a verse.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Interrupting would look like despising ה׳'s rebuke.

steps.title: No blessing over a calamity
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש gives a different reason. A new reader would have to make a ברכה right on the curses, and we do not make a ברכה over פורענות.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said: Because one does not say a blessing over calamity.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש offers a second, separate reason for the same rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each עולה says a ברכה before and after his reading. If the קללות were split, a ברכה would be said right next to the curses. That is like blessing over disaster, which is not proper.

keyTerms.meaning: we do not say a blessing

phrases.english: Reish Lakish said:

phrases.aramaic: לְפִי שֶׁאֵין אוֹמְרִים בְּרָכָה עַל הַפּוּרְעָנוּת:
phrases.english: Because one does not say a blessing over calamity.

steps.triggerLanguage: רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ אָמַר: לְפִי שֶׁאֵין אוֹמְרִים בְּרָכָה עַל הַפּוּרְעָנוּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second answer to step 19, different from רבי אסי's verse.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A ברכה may not be said directly on verses of calamity.

steps.title: So how is it done?
steps.stepSummary: Since a ברכה cannot be said on the curses, the גמרא asks how the reading is actually done.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, how does one do it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a practical question that grows out of ריש לקיש's reason. This sets up the ברייתא in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone still has to make a ברכה before and after reading the קללות. So how does he avoid making it 'on' the curses?

phrases.english: Rather, how does one do it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how the reading works in practice given ריש לקיש's reason.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How the reader avoids a ברכה directly on the curses.

steps.title: Start before the curses and end after them
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that the reader begins one פסוק before the קללות and ends one פסוק after them.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: When he begins, he begins with the verse before them, and when he finishes, he finishes with the verse after them.
steps.whatsHappening: A ברייתא answers the practical question from step 22.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By adding a פסוק before and a פסוק after, neither ברכה sits directly on a curse. The ברכות are attached to the neutral verses around the קללות.

phrases.aramaic: תָּנָא: כְּשֶׁהוּא מַתְחִיל — מַתְחִיל בַּפָּסוּק שֶׁלִּפְנֵיהֶם,
phrases.english: It was taught: When he begins, he begins with the verse before them,
and when he finishes, he finishes with the verse after them.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנָא: כְּשֶׁהוּא מַתְחִיל מַתְחִיל בַּפָּסוּק שֶׁלִּפְנֵיהֶם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 22 with a ברייתא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Begin one verse before the קללות and end one verse after them.

steps.title: אביי limits the rule to the curses in ויקרא
steps.stepSummary: אביי says the rule against interrupting applies only to the קללות in תורת כהנים. The קללות in משנה תורה may be split.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: They taught this only about the curses in תורת כהנים, but the curses in משנה תורה, one may interrupt.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי narrows the משנה's rule. It does not apply to every set of curses in the Torah.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two big sets of curses: in ויקרא (בחוקותי) and in דברים (כי תבוא). אביי says only the ויקרא curses must be read without a break. The דברים curses may be split between readers.

keyTerms.meaning: he may stop, he may interrupt

steps.confusionAlert: תורת כהנים here means ספר ויקרא, and משנה תורה means ספר דברים. It does not mean the רמב״ם's sefer.

phrases.english: Abaye said: They taught this
only about the curses in Toras Kohanim (Vayikra),
but with the curses in Mishneh Torah (Devarim), one may interrupt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the scope of the משנה's rule from step 18.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only the curses in ויקרא may not be interrupted. Those in דברים may be.

steps.title: Why the difference?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the two sets of curses are treated differently.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the reason behind אביי's distinction. This sets up the explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sets are curses in the Torah, so why are they treated differently? The גמרא wants to know what makes them different.

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind אביי's distinction.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the curses of ויקרא differ from those of דברים.

steps.title: Plural from ה׳ versus singular from משה
steps.stepSummary: The ויקרא curses are in plural and משה said them from ה׳'s mouth. The דברים curses are in singular and משה said them on his own.
steps.simpleTranslation: These are said in the plural, and משה said them from the mouth of the Almighty. Those are said in the singular, and משה said them on his own.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the ויקרא curses are more serious and so must not be broken up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ויקרא curses speak to the whole nation (plural) and come straight from ה׳, so they are harsher. The דברים curses speak to each person (singular), and משה said them in his own words. They are less severe, so it is fine to split them between readers.

keyTerms.meaning: from the mouth of the Almighty
on his own, in his own words

steps.whatToRemember: We read the ויקרא curses on a תענית without a break, for two reasons: not to despise ה׳'s rebuke (רבי אסי), and not to say a ברכה on calamity (ריש לקיש). The reader adds a verse before and after. אביי: the curses in דברים may be split, because they are in singular and משה said them himself.

phrases.english: These (in Vayikra) are said in the plural,
and Moshe said them from the mouth of the Almighty;
and those (in Devarim) are said in the singular,
and Moshe said them on his own.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 25.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ויקרא curses are plural and from ה׳, so they are harsher. The דברים curses are singular and said by משה himself.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Only the harsher curses of ויקרא must be read without interruption.

steps.title: רב הונא lets a nervous reader stop in the middle of the curses
steps.stepSummary: A story: לוי בר בוטי was stammering while reading the curses before רב הונא. רב הונא told him he could stop, because the no-interruption rule applies only to the curses in תורת כהנים, not the ones in משנה תורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: לוי בר בוטי was reading in front of רב הונא and was stammering over the curses. רב הונא told him: 'As you wish, you may stop.' The rule against stopping was taught only for the curses in ויקרא. For the curses in דברים, a reader may stop.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a real-life story that matches אביי's rule from earlier. A reader had trouble with the curses in דברים, and רב הונא allowed him to stop partway through.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 24, אביי said that only the curses in תורת כהנים may not be split. This story shows the same rule used in practice: רב הונא let the reader stop in the middle of the curses in משנה תורה. The wording is almost the same as אביי's, but here it serves as a practical ruling in a real case.

keyTerms.meaning: the curses (literally, the 'cursed ones'), meaning the תוכחה portion
as you wish; it is up to you

steps.confusionAlert: רב הונא's words repeat אביי's rule from Step 24 almost word for word. This is not a new rule. The גמרא is showing the same rule being applied in a real case.

phrases.english: Levi bar Buti was reading [from the Torah]

phrases.aramaic: וְקָא מְגַמְגֵּם קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב הוּנָא בַּאֲרוּרֵי.
phrases.english: and he was stammering before Rav Huna in the curses.
phrases.notes: The harsh words of the curses were hard for him to say.

phrases.english: He said to him: As you wish [you may stop].
phrases.notes: Another person can continue the reading.

phrases.aramaic: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא קְלָלוֹת שֶׁבְּתוֹרַת כֹּהֲנִים,
phrases.english: They only taught [the rule] about the curses in Leviticus,
but for those in Deuteronomy, one may stop.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֵוִי בַּר בּוּטֵי הֲוָה קָרֵי וְקָא מְגַמְגֵּם קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב הוּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a practical story that matches אביי's distinction between the two sets of curses.
steps.raayaObject: אביי's rule that the curses in משנה תורה may be interrupted
steps.raayaSupportSource: The story of רב הונא and לוי בר בוטי

steps.title: Ezra set the times for reading the two sets of curses
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר says עזרא enacted that the curses in תורת כהנים be read before עצרת, and the curses in משנה תורה before ראש השנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in a ברייתא: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר says: עזרא enacted for the Jewish people that they read the curses in ויקרא before שבועות, and the curses in דברים before ראש השנה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new source about the timing of the curses. עזרא arranged the yearly reading so that each set of curses falls just before a certain holiday.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The topic shifts from how the curses are read to when they are read. The schedule is a תקנה made by עזרא. It ties the curses in ויקרא (בחוקותי) to עצרת and the curses in דברים (כי תבוא) to ראש השנה.

keyTerms.meaning: it was taught in a ברייתא
עזרא enacted, made a rabbinic arrangement

phrases.aramaic: תַּנְיָא, רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: It was taught: Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar says:
Ezra enacted for the Jewish people

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁיְּהוּ קוֹרִין קְלָלוֹת שֶׁבְּתוֹרַת כֹּהֲנִים קוֹדֶם עֲצֶרֶת,
phrases.english: that they should read the curses in Leviticus before Shavuot,
and those in Deuteronomy before Rosh HaShana.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא, רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר אוֹמֵר: עֶזְרָא תִּיקֵּן לָהֶן לְיִשְׂרָאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the topic of interrupting the curses to the topic of when they are read.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The curses in ויקרא are read before עצרת, and the curses in דברים are read before ראש השנה, by תקנת עזרא.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for our custom of reading בחוקותי before שבועות and כי תבוא before ראש השנה.

steps.title: Why did Ezra set this timing?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason behind עזרא's schedule.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a short question to set up the next step: why should the curses come right before these holidays?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא gave the rule but no reason. The גמרא wants to know the idea behind placing the curses at these points in the year.

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the ברייתא in Step 28.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason for reading the curses right before עצרת and ראש השנה.

steps.title: So that the year ends together with its curses
steps.stepSummary: אביי (or רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ) explains: the curses are read at the end of the year so the year and its curses finish together.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said, and some say it was ריש לקיש: so that the year may end together with its curses.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the reason for עזרא's schedule. Reading the curses at the close of the year is like a prayer that the bad things end with that year, and the new year starts fresh.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Placing the curses at the very end of the year symbolically 'closes them out.' This makes clear sense for ראש השנה. Whether it also fits עצרת is the question the גמרא raises next.

keyTerms.meaning: and some say; the statement is attributed to someone else
that the year may end together with its curses

phrases.english: Abaye said, and some say it was Reish Lakish:
So that the year may end along with its curses.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 29.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The curses are read before the new year so that the old year and its curses end together.

steps.title: But is שבועות a new year?
steps.stepSummary: The reason fits ראש השנה, but for the curses in תורת כהנים read before עצרת, the reason seems not to work, since עצרת is not a new year.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense for the curses in דברים, because there 'the year ends with its curses' fits. But for the curses in ויקרא, is שבועות a new year?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the reason just given. It works for ראש השנה but seems not to explain the reading before שבועות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'end of the year' reason requires that a new year begin right after the reading. ראש השנה clearly marks a new year, but עצרת does not seem to. So the reason appears to explain only half of עזרא's enactment.

keyTerms.meaning: is that to say? (a challenging question)

phrases.english: Granted, the ones in Deuteronomy:
there is [the reason] 'so the year may end with its curses.'
But the ones in Leviticus,
is that to say Shavuot is a new year?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reason given in Step 30 as it applies to עצרת.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reason 'so the year may end with its curses' as applied to the reading before עצרת
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The reason only works before a new year, and עצרת does not seem to be a new year.

steps.title: Yes, שבועות is a new year for fruit trees
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that עצרת is also a kind of ראש השנה, as the משנה says that on עצרת the world is judged for the fruit of the trees.
steps.simpleTranslation: Yes, שבועות is also a new year, as we learned in a משנה: 'And on עצרת [the world is judged] for the fruit of the trees.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. It shows from a משנה in ראש השנה that עצרת is a judgment day, which makes it a kind of new year.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה in מסכת ראש השנה lists four judgment times in the year, and עצרת is when tree fruit is judged. A day of judgment counts as a 'new year' for that area. So the reason 'end the year with its curses' fits עצרת too.

keyTerms.meaning: as we learned in a משנה

steps.confusionAlert: This does not mean שבועות is the calendar new year. It means that שבועות is a day of judgment for tree fruit, and in that sense it begins a new 'year.'
steps.whatToRemember: עזרא placed the curses before עצרת and before ראש השנה, because both are days of judgment. Reading the curses right before them lets the year end along with its curses.

phrases.aramaic: אִין, עֲצֶרֶת נָמֵי רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה הִיא.
phrases.english: Yes, Shavuot is also a new year.
As we learned: 'And on Shavuot [judgment is] for the fruit of the tree.'
phrases.notes: From the משנה in ראש השנה 16a.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִין, עֲצֶרֶת נָמֵי רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 31.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefinition supported by a source: עצרת is shown to be a judgment day, which makes it a new year in a real sense.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Only ראש השנה is a new year, so the reason seems not to apply to עצרת.
steps.terutzMaskana: עצרת is a judgment day for tree fruit, so it is also a ראש השנה, and the reason applies there too.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Both readings of the curses come right before a day of judgment.

steps.title: The tearing down of elders is building; the building of youths is tearing down
steps.stepSummary: A second ברייתא from רבי שמעון בן אלעזר: if elders say 'tear down' and youths say 'build,' follow the elders.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר says: If elders tell you 'tear down' and youths tell you 'build,' tear down and do not build. This is because the tearing down of elders is really building, and the building of youths is really tearing down.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another teaching from the same תנא, רבי שמעון בן אלעזר, as is common. This is a lesson about wisdom, not a law about reading the Torah.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The point is that experience matters more than how the advice looks. Advice from elders that looks destructive often leads to lasting good. Advice from inexperienced youths that looks constructive often leads to ruin.

keyTerms.meaning: elders, people with age and experience

steps.confusionAlert: This teaching is placed here because it is from the same תנא, רבי שמעון בן אלעזר. It is not connected to the topic of the curses.

phrases.aramaic: תַּנְיָא, רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: It was taught: Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar says:
If elders say to you 'Demolish'
and youths [say] 'Build' —
demolish and do not build,
because the demolishing of elders is building,
and the building of youths is demolishing.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא, רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר אוֹמֵר: אִם יֹאמְרוּ לָךְ זְקֵנִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new teaching brought because it comes from the same תנא as the ברייתא in Step 28.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Follow the advice of experienced elders over that of youths, even when the elders' advice looks destructive.

steps.title: רחבעם בן שלמה as the example
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא gives רחבעם as an example: he rejected the elders' advice, followed the youths, and lost most of his kingdom.
steps.simpleTranslation: And a sign for this is רחבעם, the son of שלמה.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא ends by pointing to a story from Tanach that proves the lesson. רחבעם listened to the young men instead of the elders, and the kingdom split.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In מלכים א פרק יב, the elders told רחבעם to humble himself before the people. That looked like 'tearing down' his authority. The youths told him to act harshly, which looked like 'building' his power. He followed the youths, and ten tribes broke away.

keyTerms.meaning: a sign or illustration for the matter
רחבעם, the son of King שלמה

steps.whatToRemember: Experienced advice that looks like 'tearing down' really builds, and youthful advice that looks like 'building' really destroys, as the story of רחבעם shows.

phrases.english: And an indication of the matter: Rehoboam son of Solomon.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a historical example for the lesson in Step 33.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that the 'building' of youths is really destruction
steps.raayaSupportSource: The story of רחבעם in מלכים א פרק יב, where the kingdom split

steps.title: רבי מאיר: each reading picks up where the last one ended
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא brings רבי מאיר's view: every reading continues forward from the exact place the previous reading stopped.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: wherever they stop reading on שבת morning, that is where they start at שבת מנחה. Where they stop at מנחה, they start on Monday. Where they stop on Monday, they start on Thursday. Where they stop on Thursday, they start on the next שבת. These are the words of רבי מאיר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא that discusses where the Torah reading resumes during the week. This first part gives רבי מאיר's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי מאיר, the readings form a chain. Each one moves the place in the תורה forward, so שבת מנחה, Monday, and Thursday each cover new verses. The next שבת then starts wherever Thursday stopped.

keyTerms.meaning: The Rabbis taught. This phrase opens a ברייתא.
They stop or end the reading.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
The place where they stop on Shabbat morning —
there they read at the afternoon service;
where they stop at the afternoon service, there they read on Monday;
where they stop on Monday, there they read on Thursday;
where they stop on Thursday, there they read on the coming Shabbat;
these are the words of Rabbi Meir.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: מָקוֹם שֶׁמַּפְסִיקִין בַּשַּׁבָּת שַׁחֲרִית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic after the discussion of the curses and רחבעם. It moves to the order of the weekly Torah readings.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי מאיר, each reading resumes where the previous one ended, moving forward continuously.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: all the readings start from where שבת morning ended
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה holds that שבת מנחה, Monday, Thursday, and the next שבת all begin from the place where שבת morning stopped.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: wherever they stop on שבת morning, that is where they start at מנחה, on Monday, on Thursday, and on the next שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא now gives the opposing view, from רבי יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יהודה, the readings do not advance during the week. The spot where שבת morning ended stays the starting point for every reading until the next שבת morning. Only then does the full reading move on.

keyTerms.meaning: רבי יהודה says. This introduces the disagreeing view.
Monday, the second day of the week
Thursday, the fifth day of the week

steps.confusionAlert: Under רבי יהודה, Monday and Thursday do not continue from where מנחה stopped. They go back to the same starting point, so the opening verses are read again each time.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:
The place where they stop on Shabbat morning —
there they read at the afternoon service,
and on Monday and on Thursday, and on the coming Shabbat.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: מָקוֹם שֶׁמַּפְסִיקִין בַּשַּׁבָּת שַׁחֲרִית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the view that disagrees with רבי מאיר in the same ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יהודה, all readings until the next שבת morning start from where שבת morning ended.

steps.title: רבי זירא rules by spelling out the full rule
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא states the הלכה. It matches רבי יהודה's view, but he writes out the whole rule instead of naming רבי יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said: the הלכה is that wherever they stop on שבת morning, that is where they start at מנחה, on Monday, on Thursday, and on the next שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא gives the final ruling, which matches the second view in the ברייתא. Notice that he repeats the whole rule word for word, because the גמרא is about to ask about this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The content of the ruling is exactly what רבי יהודה said. What stands out is the way it is said: רבי זירא does not just write "the הלכה follows רבי יהודה." This unusual wording sets up the next question.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who gives the practical ruling here
The practical law, how we actually act

steps.whyThisMatters: This is how we practice: the weekday and שבת מנחה readings repeat the opening of the next week's portion, and they do not advance.

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said: The halakha is:
The place where they stop on Shabbat morning —
there they read at the afternoon service,
and on Monday and on Thursday, and on the coming Shabbat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Decides the מחלוקת in practice, matching the content of רבי יהודה's view.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The הלכה is that all readings until the next שבת start from where שבת morning ended.

steps.title: Why not just say the law follows רבי יהודה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי זירא's wording: if he agrees with רבי יהודה, he should simply say so.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let him just say: the הלכה is like רבי יהודה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why רבי זירא spelled out the whole rule when a short "like רבי יהודה" would have been enough. The answer comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally, when an אמורא agrees with one side of a מחלוקת, he just names that תנא. Repeating the whole rule suggests there is a reason for it, perhaps doubt about who said which view. The גמרא is pressing on this wording.

keyTerms.meaning: So let him say. This is a challenge to someone's choice of words.
The הלכה follows the view of a named sage

phrases.english: So let him say: The halakha is in accordance with Rabbi Yehuda!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the long wording of רבי זירא's ruling in step 37.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי זירא's choice to repeat the full rule instead of naming רבי יהודה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The content is identical to רבי יהודה's view, so the extra wording seems unnecessary. Normally one would just say "the הלכה follows רבי יהודה."
